From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PulseWide — multiple extension requests flagged (logs attached)

Team,

FYI I'm seeing a cluster of extension/credit requests from PulseWide over the last 10 days across at least four distinct accounts (same billing domain). They asked our SDRs for additional trial credits 3x in rapid succession and then submitted a request_deck to request more seats. Billing flagged some overlapping payment attempts.

I attached a quick CSV with the ticket/credit request timestamps and account ids (pulsewide_extension_log.csv). Can security or fraud take a quick look before we reply? I haven't promised anything.

Quick summary:
- First extension: 2027-06-05 (account pw-team-a)
- Second extension: 2027-06-10 (pw-team-b)
- Third extension: 2027-06-12 (pw-contractors)
- New request received today for a company-wide extension

Asking: do we treat this as coordinated abuse or a legitimate multi-team pilot?

Thanks,
Ben
--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PulseWide — multiple extension requests flagged (logs attached)

Thanks Ben — received.

I pulled the CSV; there are some clear signals that justify a short hold: same invoice domain, overlapping IPs during initial signup windows, and two accounts created within 48 hrs of each other. That pattern has correlated with credit-cycling in the past.

Action I propose:
1) Do not grant any further trial credits until we hear directly from the primary PulseWide admin with org-level verification (incorporation docs or proof of centralized billing).
2) Ask CS (Marissa) to pause any outbound promises and escalate the external request to me.
3) Rishi: can you run a quick cross-account similarity check (device/IP, payment fingerprint) and surface anything high-risk?

Ben — we should acknowledge the customer request without committing to credits. I can draft a response that requests that evidence.

-Neha

Hi Alicia — thanks for the deck and the explanation. Appreciate the transparency.

We want to make sure we handle this carefully — we protect trial credits to avoid large-scale abuse and to be fair to other customers. Before we can approve a blanket one-week extension across accounts, we need a quick verification so we can tie the accounts together on our side. Could you provide any of the following (whichever is easiest):

- A single purchase order or procurement contact that will consolidate the pilot 
- Confirmation of centralized billing (billing@pulsewide.io) and the PO number you expect to use
- Company incorporation (or VAT) number and a plain statement that the three accounts are internal teams under one legal entity

If you can send a single confirmation email from your finance/procurement alias (billing@pulsewide.io) that authorizes a coordinated, one-week extension for these pilot accounts, we can fast-track review.

Separately, internally we are doing a quick risk check. I may reach out with a short follow-up for IP/payment artifacts.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Risk & Trust Operations, Redwood Inference

Quick update from the similarity check:
- Payment fingerprints: 2 distinct cards, both tied to the same billing domain but one card reused across two accounts.
- Signup IPs: overlap between pw-team-a and pw-contractors during signup (same /24 block).
- Device fingerprints: several shared UA strings and identical timezone settings for 5 of the 6 primary users.

Risk call: medium. Behaviors are consistent with decentralized teams testing legitimately, but the reused card and IP overlap raise the possibility of credit sharing or quota cycling if we grant new free credits broadly.

Recommendation: deny blanket extension request until we receive confirmation from a centralized billing contact. If procurement confirms, we can either:
A) Grant a one-time consolidated extension (manual approval) or
B) Offer a short paid pilot with upfront invoice and a small credit applied on payment (preferred — reduces abuse vector).

Rishi
Senior Fraud Analyst, Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia — and thanks again for the quick follow-up.

After an internal review (see Rishi's notes), we can't approve a blanket extension across multiple accounts purely on the basis of team-level ad-hoc signups. The reuse of a billing instrument across accounts and the signup IP overlap mean there's a material risk of credit-cycling.

That said, we want to help PulseWide evaluate Redwood in a way that protects both sides. Two options we can do quickly:

1) One-time consolidated extension: your finance/procurement team (billing@pulsewide.io) sends an authorization email confirming the three pilot accounts are under the same legal entity and requesting a coordinated one-week extension. We'll then apply credits to the consolidated org-level pilot.

2) Preferred: Short paid pilot — we issue an invoice for a small pilot seat bundle (30-day), apply a $X0 credit on receipt of payment, and extend support for onboarding. This eliminates the abuse vector and gets you predictable capacity.

If you'd like, I can draft a mutual action plan and a PO-friendly invoice now; attaching a short MAP template (MAP-pulsewide-v1.docx) to speed procurement.

Please let me know which route you prefer. If you choose the consolidated extension, please have billing@pulsewide.io confirm in a reply to this thread.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Risk & Trust Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-pulsewide-v1.docx]
